candidate_sentences.text: Total revenue for the year reached 53.2 million euros, representing a substantial increase compared to 18.2 million euros in the previous year.
Gross profit for 2025 climbed to 18.8 million euros with a gross margin of 35 percent, compared with 5.4 million euros and a 30 percent margin in 2024.
Operating profit surged to 14.7 million euros, yielding an operating margin of 28 percent, a sharp rise from 0.1 million euros the prior year.
The company recorded a net profit of 12.0 million euros for the twelve months of 2025, representing a strong turnaround from the net loss of 3.9 million euros reported in 2024.
Basic earnings per share rose accordingly to 0.22 euros for the year, compared with a loss of 0.06 euros in the previous period.
Total assets increased to 124.5 million euros as of 31 December 2025, up from 118.8 million euros a year earlier, while total liabilities decreased to 61.2 million euros from 67.5 million euros.
Total equity grew to 63.3 million euros, lifting the net asset value per share to 1.12 euros from 0.89 euros.
The debt-to-equity ratio improved to 0.97 from 1.32 at the end of 2024.
Operating cash flow turned positive, generating 10.8 million euros during 2025 compared to a cash outflow of 10.4 million euros in the prior year.

verified_key_information_units.information: Revenue growth was primarily driven by the handover of completed residential units in the Kalaranna District and Uus-Kindrali developments in Tallinn, as well as the City Villas project in Vilnius, contrasting lower 2024 revenue due to delayed starts in Kalaranna and limited sales elsewhere.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management report - Revenue from real estate sales section

candidate_sentences.text: The revenue growth was primarily powered by real estate sales amounting to 45.4 million euros, up from 10.7 million euros in 2024, as completed apartments were successfully handed over to buyers.
In Tallinn, construction was completed on the white building at the Uus-Kindrali project and the Kalaranna District, directly driving revenue through apartment handovers.

verified_key_information_units.information: Segmental revenue shifted significantly, with Estonia contributing 75% of total revenue in 2025 (versus 27% in 2024), Latvia's contribution falling to 0.3% (from 25%), and Lithuania maintaining a stable 12% share (versus 11% in 2024).
Liquidity and capital position improved, supported by active management of bank loans and bonds.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Key performance indicators table; Financing sources and policies section

candidate_sentences.text: Total assets increased to 124.5 million euros as of 31 December 2025, up from 118.8 million euros a year earlier, while total liabilities decreased to 61.2 million euros from 67.5 million euros.
The debt-to-equity ratio improved to 0.97 from 1.32 at the end of 2024.
Capital structure management included the partial redemption of secured non-convertible bonds by 9.4 million euros, reducing the outstanding nominal bond amount to 10.5 million euros by year-end.

verified_key_information_units.information: Major real estate developments advanced: completion of the white building in Uus-Kindrali (Tallinn) with 39 units closed by year-end (78% of sellable area sold); construction commenced on the Blue Marine project in Riga's Klīversala Quarter; first real rights agreements signed and units handed over in Šaltinių Namai Attico (Vilnius); and building permit obtained for the Borgo luxury residential complex in Vilnius (construction planned for H2 2026).

In Vilnius, construction neared completion on the final stage of Šaltinių Namai Attico with City Villas, with customer handovers beginning in December 2025.

details.coherence_justification: The candidate summary is fully coherent internally. All statements are logically connected and support the overall narrative of strong financial performance in 2025. There are no self-contradictions, logical gaps, or organizational problems. The summary flows logically from revenue growth to profitability metrics, then to balance sheet strength and operational highlights, concluding with a single impairment charge that is properly contextualized as an isolated event. The financial metrics consistently show improvement year-over-year without any arithmetic contradictions, and operational updates are clearly organized by location. There is no unnecessary repetition that would reduce clarity.
